newsitem.title: USA: Witness first thought accused Mass. nanny was hero.
newsitem.headline: Witness first thought accused Mass. nanny was hero.

text.p: The first witness to testify on Wednesday in a pre-trial court hearing for the British au pair accused of killing a 9-month-old baby said at first he thought she was "a borderline hero."
The hearing is examining a request by the defence to limit the evidence against defendant Louise Woodward.

Newton Police Sgt. William Byrne Jr. testified that after 10 minutes of questioning Woodward about the injuries suffered by Matthew Eappen he thought, "she may have been a borderline hero ... she may have tried to revive the baby that had gone unconscious."
But that thought was shattered when doctors at Children's Hospital in Boston told him the head injuries suffered could not have been accidentally sustained.
Under questioning by prosecutor Lynn Rooney, the 23-year police veteran said Woodward "seemed remarkably calm."

Woodward, who had been told by police that the baby was very ill, told the officers he woke up crying and had been cranky all day. She also told them she had felt angry and frustrated by the baby's continuing cries, Byrne testified.
Woodward admitted she "dropped the baby on the floor" and "tossed the baby on the bed," Byrne said.

When she went to change the infant's diapers in the afternoon, she noticed "his eyes rolling back in his head and his head rolling backward," he said. She tried to call the baby's parents, who are both doctors, and when she was unable to reach them called the police emergency number.
Woodward, now 19, from Chester, England, is facing murder charges in the infant's February 1997 death.
